bull.b: Low leverage reduces refinancing pressure and preserves financial flexibility while the higher reported equity base provides stronger capitalization. This gives Artiva more capacity to fund development activities and absorb volatility than a similarly loss-making biotech with heavier debt.

Director elections extending through 2029 provide board continuity during a critical development stage, while auditor ratification supports established financial oversight. Stable governance can help maintain execution discipline and investor confidence as the company pursues its programs.

Additional equity compensation capacity can help a development-stage biotech recruit and retain specialized employees when cash resources are constrained. Preserving scientific and operating talent is important for maintaining program execution and advancing the business over multiple quarters.

bear.b: The disappearance of revenue leaves Artiva without a commercial base to offset research and operating costs. Sustained zero revenue means progress depends on advancing development programs toward future commercialization, making near-term financial performance highly vulnerable to execution delays.

Persistent losses indicate that current operations are not yet generating economic returns and that substantial spending continues without a revenue offset. Unless development efforts create a commercial revenue stream, these losses will keep weighing on capital efficiency and financial sustainability.

bear.t: Heavy Cash Burn and Funding Dependence
bear.b: Cash consumption at this level can shorten the period covered by existing resources and increase dependence on future financing. External funding needs may constrain strategic flexibility, especially because ongoing losses translate into actual cash outflows rather than mainly non-cash expenses.
